subject.title: fix(ui): preserve login across same-origin gateways

question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR's browser credential migration policy where the first opened gateway claims the legacy unscoped device-auth store and then removes that ambiguous key?
rationale: The code appears to fix the same-origin collision cleanly, but it changes shipped browser credential storage and upgrade behavior for existing profiles, which is a maintainer-owned auth/security boundary choice.

options.title: Accept Scoped Migration
options.body: Proceed with this PR after exact-head CI if maintainers accept endpoint-scoped device credentials and first-gateway legacy claim/delete as the upgrade boundary.

options.title: Require Different Legacy Handling
options.body: Ask for a narrower migration if maintainers want to preserve or defer ambiguous legacy credentials instead of assigning them to the first opened gateway.

options.title: Split Remaining Mobile Auth Work
options.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99903 separate because this PR fixes same-origin credential collision, not Android background storage loss.

recommendation.title: Accept Scoped Migration
recommendation.body: Proceed with this PR after exact-head CI if maintainers accept endpoint-scoped device credentials and first-gateway legacy claim/delete as the upgrade boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest recent owner for Control UI storage upgrade policy from the merged base-path settings isolation work and CODEOWNERS context.
